newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian presidential election called for June 15.
newsitem.headline: Croatian presidential election called for June 15.

text.p: The Croatian government on Monday set June 15 as the date for presidential elections in which President Franjo Tudjman has said he will run as candidate for the ruling Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ).
Although reported to be seriously ill, Tudjman, 74, still enjoys huge popularity in the country and is widely expected to romp home in the polls for another five-year term.

A statement issued at the weekend by the medical team treating the president said he was in excellent health and his treatment has been successful. But observers say he has been battling cancer since last year when he was treated in a U.S. hospital and is unlikely to last another full term.
The opposition is badly divided and so far only the leader of the Social Liberal Party, Vlado Gotovac, has indicated that he will run in the election.

"The Croatian government made a unanimous decision in today's session to call the elections for the president of the Republic of Croatia for June 15 this year," the government said in a statement to Croatia media.
Tudjman was elected president on August 2, 1992 with 56 percent of the vote. His popularity remains high despite allegations of corruption within his party.
The HDZ has lost some support but still did suprisingly well in local elections in April, when it regained or held majorities in most county assemblies and town councils.
Known as the "Father of the Nation" for declaring Croatian independence in 1991, Tudjman then led his country in a bitter war which spread throughout the former Yugoslavia.
If he wins, Tudjman will preside over the recovery of the last piece of Croatian territory taken by Serbs in 1991 when Croatia seceded from Yugoslavia.
Eastern Slavonia has been under United Nations administration since January last year and Tudjman is bound to treat its reintegration as a major victory for independent Croatia.
